h: Getting the Best From Your Wax-Work Adventure
p: Madame Tussauds London sits on Marylebone Road, one of the busiest roads in central London, and its distinctive green dome is hard to miss. Once you're inside, it's a world of famous faces, from Hollywood royalty to real royalty, sports legends and pop superstars. It's all designed for getting up close, so be ready to strike a pose.

Timing is everything here. It's a hugely popular attraction, especially during school holidays and at weekends, so booking a timed entry and arriving early in the day helps. Weekday mornings in term time tend to be calmer, which makes it easier to get the photos you want without a queue behind you.

Think about what you'd like to see before you go. The line-up changes as new figures are added, and there are often themed areas linked to films, music and sport. If you've got a particular hero in mind, it's worth checking which figures are on display before your visit, as favourites do come and go.

After your visit, there's plenty nearby. Regent's Park is a short walk away, with its boating lake, gardens and the famous Queen Mary's Rose Garden. ZSL London Zoo is on the north side of the park, making a great add-on for families. And Marylebone High Street has a lovely mix of independent shops and cafés, perfect for a sit-down after all those selfies.
